title: Implement hard min/max bounds enforcement in Dedicated autoscaler loop
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
Dedicated customers need contractual/operational guardrails for spend + SLOs. This ticket implements hard enforcement of customer-configured min/max replicas (or GPU-equivalent units) in the autoscaler decision loop. Bounds must have deterministic semantics, never be violated, and be visible via metrics/logs.

Scope
- Clamp autoscaler desired capacity to configured bounds (min_replicas <= desired <= max_replicas).
- Ensure bounds take precedence over platform defaults (but do not override safety constraints like "scale-up blocked by fleet shortage"—instead surface degraded/unmet-min state).
- Emit metrics and structured logs explaining (a) requested desired, (b) bounded desired, and (c) reason for clamp.
- Integrate with cooldown/anti-oscillation guardrails (separate ticket may implement dampening; this ticket must not regress those semantics).
- Backward compatible: feature does nothing unless scaling_policy bounds are present/enabled per account/deployment.

Non-goals
- Designing the control plane schema/Console UX (see ENG-22141 + design spec).
- Implementing predictive scaling signals (see ENG-22142).
- Cross-region capacity placement.

Design/ADR links
- ADR (precedence + safety invariants): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json
- Design spec (schema + UX semantics): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/autoscaling-policy-schema-and-console-ux.json
- Autoscaler/predictive architecture: sources/confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/autoscaler-bounds-and-predictive-signals-architecture.json
- Metric naming standards: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/metric-naming-for-scaling-and-capacity.json

Proposed implementation (high level)
1) Fetch effective scaling policy
- Autoscaler reads effective policy from control plane cache (policy service), including:
  - min_replicas, max_replicas
  - cooldowns and scale-down safety baseline (if present)
  - enablement flag (account/deployment)
- If bounds not present OR feature flag off: keep existing behavior.

2) Decision pipeline changes
- Existing pipeline (simplified):
  - reactive_signals -> desired_raw -> cooldown/dampening -> desired
- New pipeline (with bounds):
  - reactive_signals -> desired_raw
  - apply cooldown/dampening -> desired_unbounded
  - clamp to bounds -> desired_bounded
  - emit metrics/logs/audit trail inputs
  - pass to provisioning layer
- Precedence:
  - Bounds are hard clamps.
  - Reactive safety overrides (e.g., high queue depth / saturation) can increase desired_unbounded but still cannot exceed max.
  - Scale-down cannot go below min.

3) Determinism + auditability
- Each autoscaler iteration should produce a stable explanation string/enum (no free-form data-dependent ordering).
- Persist (or emit) the following:
  - desired_unbounded
  - desired_bounded
  - clamp_reason: NONE | CLAMPED_TO_MIN | CLAMPED_TO_MAX
  - inputs snapshot: key signal summaries (queue depth, utilization, p95 latency, etc.)

4) Region capacity shortage behavior (interaction)
- If min cannot be met due to fleet capacity shortage:
  - desired_bounded remains >= min (desired intent), but provisioning returns "unmet" state.
  - Autoscaler should NOT thrash; retry w/ backoff + surface degraded state.
  - Alerting + customer messaging handled in ENG-22151 / PR-48270.

Acceptance criteria
- Safety invariants:
  - Never request provisioning above max when bounds enabled.
  - Never request provisioning below min when bounds enabled.
  - When bounds disabled: behavior identical to current autoscaler.
- Observability:
  - Metrics for desired_unbounded vs desired_bounded exist and are queryable per deployment_id + region.
  - Counter for clamp events (to min/max) exists.
  - Structured log includes clamp_reason and both desired values.
- Testing:
  - Unit tests cover: min>desired, desired>max, min==max, missing bounds, bounds disabled.
  - Integration test covers end-to-end clamp + metric emission.
  - Regression tests ensure cooldown behavior unchanged.
- Rollout readiness:
  - Gated by feature flag (account/deployment).
  - Canary deploy in one region with 1 pilot account before expanding.

Subtasks
- [x] Implement clamp function and ensure it is applied after cooldown/dampening.
- [x] Add clamp_reason enum + plumb through autoscaler decision object.
- [x] Add metrics:
  - desired_replicas_unbounded
  - desired_replicas_bounded
  - bound_hit_total{bound="min"|"max"}
- [x] Add structured logs for each scaling decision (include deployment_id, region, desired values, clamp_reason).
- [x] Add unit tests for clamp edge cases.
- [x] Add integration test that asserts bound_hit_total increments.
- [x] Verify metric naming + label cardinality against observability standards.
- [x] Validate behavior with simulation replay harness (quick pass) for a max-bound saturation scenario.

Risks / notes
- Oscillation risk: if upstream desired_unbounded is noisy, clamp-to-max can create perceived "stuck" behavior and persistent queueing. Must ensure we emit explicit bounded-state signals so routing/SRE can respond (see PR-48345).
- Cardinality risk: metrics must not label on customer_name; use customer_id/deployment_id per standards and confirm cardinality budgets.
- Behavioral changes at boundaries: scale-down to min can hide inefficiency; ensure Console surfaces "recommended" ranges separately (ENG-22150).
- Shortage semantics: do not silently violate min; instead report unmet-min and alert.

Implementation references (PRs)
- Control plane fields: sources/github/redwood/pr-48211-add-scaling-policy-schema-min-max-bounds.json
- Bounds enforcement (this ticket): sources/github/redwood/pr-48218-enforce-min-max-bounds-in-dedicated-autoscaler.json
- Metrics/structured logs: sources/github/redwood/pr-48241-add-metrics-desired-vs-bounded-capacity.json
- Cooldowns/anti-oscillation (related): sources/github/redwood/pr-48288-add-cooldown-and-anti-oscillation-guardrails.json

Release/rollout notes
- This change is safe to ship behind feature flag even before Console UX lands; policy can be set by internal admin tooling.
- Coordinate enablement with SRE for pilot accounts; ensure dashboards include bound hit rate before turning on.

2025-06-23 (Jordan Lee): Please ensure determinism in reason strings for auditability. Prefer enum for clamp_reason; log signal summary in stable key order.

2025-07-16 (Vanessa Ortiz): Merged pr-48218 + pr-48241. Next: canary enablement for Hexagon in us-east (coordinate with Rafael). Please make sure dashboards show bounded vs unbounded for rapid diagnosis.
